n: A trustworthy saying: wanting to serve as a bishop is wanting a good work. In the early Church, the bishop was an overseer who presided over a local congregation.

f.g: Greek episkopos — overseer; one who watches over the flock.

n: A bishop must have an unblemished reputation, be faithful to his wife, self-controlled, sensible, respectable, welcoming, and able to teach.

f.g: A faithful, one-woman man; likely ruling out unfaithfulness or polygamy in that setting.
Temperate, clear-headed.
Skilled at teaching.

n: He must not be a heavy drinker or violent, but gentle and peaceable, not greedy or quarrelsome, and not in love with money.

f.g: Not violent, not quick to hit.
Shameful gain — dishonest money.
Quarrelsome person.

n: He must lead his own family well, with children who respect him.

f.g: Presides over, cares for.
Dignity, seriousness.

n: If a man can’t lead his own household, how can he care for God’s Church? The family is the training ground for leadership.
He must not be a new convert, or he could become conceited and fall under the same judgment as the devil, whose downfall was pride.

f.g: Literally “newly planted” — a recent convert.

n: He must also have a good reputation with outsiders, so he isn’t disgraced and trapped by the devil.

f.g: Non-members, outsiders.
Disgrace.

n: Deacons, too, must be serious and worthy of respect, honest in speech, not heavy drinkers, and not greedy.

f.g: Greek diakonoi — servants, assistants to the bishop.
Saying one thing to one person and another to someone else.

n: They must hold fast to the revealed truths of the faith with a clear conscience.

f.g: The revealed truths of the gospel.

n: They should first be tested, and if found blameless, then serve as deacons.

f.g: Tested, examined.

n: Likewise the women — likely deacons’ wives, or possibly women who served the Church — must be dignified, not gossips, self-controlled, and faithful in everything.

f.g: Greek gynaikas — “women” or “wives”; context is debated.
Greek diabolous — the word also used for “devil.”

n: Deacons must be faithful husbands who lead their children and households well.
Those who serve well as deacons earn a good standing and great confidence in their faith in Christ.

f.g: A good standing, an honorable position.
Confidence, freedom of speech.

n: Paul hopes to come to Timothy soon, but writes these instructions now.
If Paul is delayed, Timothy will know how people should conduct themselves in God’s household — the Church of the living God, which supports and upholds the truth.

f.g: God’s household or family, not a building.

f.w: pillar and ground of the truth
f.g: Support and foundation that hold truth up.

n: Paul quotes what may be an early hymn about Christ: God came in the flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, preached to the nations, believed in by the world, and taken up into glory.

f.w: God was manifest in the flesh

f.g: Vindicated — shown to be right — by the Spirit, especially in the Resurrection.
